ideas.title: Clap, and the island answers (playable)
ideas.goal: Jumped in as Lumi at night, the player presses C to clap: a ring of warm light runs out over the real ground, trees and walls in the order the sound reaches them, and every friend the sound reaches turns its head toward the clap; a friend hiding behind a bush is lit only from the side the sound can reach. Fun: a new sense you use with a key, and the night hide and seek becomes playable.
ideas.idea: My echo tracer (physics/echo.jl, acoustic rays on Raycore's BVH) built once off the frame; the key fires 10k rays, the hits glow in arrival order slowed 60x. The night around the player darkens so the ring is the brightest thing. Each creature gets the arrival time of the direct sound at its head (ray from the clap, blocked or not by the stage) and turns or flinches at that moment, a blocked one later and quieter (from the first echo path).
ideas.form: Project island-echo's next step: a plugin key and creature reactions in the human's game, and a path traced night film of the player clapping and friends turning.

ideas.title: Fireflies that learn your rhythm
ideas.goal: At dusk the player swings a lantern in a rhythm; the meadow's fireflies, each with its own little clock, start to blink with it until the whole field flashes in one wave, and the player can lead the wave across the island. Fun: a living thing you can teach, and a field-wide flash you made.
ideas.idea: Each firefly is a pulse-coupled oscillator (Mirollo-Strogatz, the model for the synchronous fireflies of the Smoky Mountains): it sees flashes of its neighbours within a few metres (and the player's lantern) and nudges its phase. A GPU kernel over a few hundred flies. Watching: scattered random sparkles that, after a minute of the lantern's beat, roll into synchronized waves.
ideas.form: A dusk game in the human's game (a key swings the lantern), and a path traced film of the field falling into step.

ideas.title: The owl that hears you
ideas.goal: At night an owl sits in the old tree and turns its head to every sound; the player must sneak a present to a sleeping friend past it. Grass is quiet, gravel and puddles are loud, and how loud a step is where the owl sits depends on what is between you. Fun: stealth by sound, where the world's shapes hide you.
ideas.idea: Footsteps are little sound sources whose loudness depends on the ground's material; the echo tracer gives how much of each step reaches the owl's two ears (time and level difference), and the owl turns its head toward the estimate, closer the louder. A generated owl asset (text -> image -> mesh).
ideas.form: A night mini game with a new creature; a path traced film of a sneak.

ideas.title: Lumi folds its wings
ideas.goal: Lumi stands like a bird: wings folded on its back, weight on one leg, a tuck of the head when it is bored, and it shakes its feathers out after landing. Fun: the lead looks alive when it does nothing, the moment players watch most.
ideas.idea: A new idle layer for Lumi's rig: wing bones folded with a spring toward the body, the T-pose gone, and the crest and wings driven by damped springs from the body's motion, so nothing flicks at 7 m/s. Its feeling (bored now) picks the idle: a slow sigh, a foot shuffle.
ideas.form: Lumi's own body and animation in the human's game; a short traced film of Lumi idling, bored, then perking up.

ideas.title: A raft you load like a puzzle
ideas.goal: The friends bring generated crates, pumpkins and logs to a raft on the pond; the player places each one, and the raft floats, tilts and sinks for real. Fill it without tipping it. Fun: a stacking puzzle where the water is the judge.
ideas.idea: Rigid bodies in PrintSim (affine bodies, IPC contact) on a buoyant raft: buoyancy from the submerged volume of the raft mesh against the pond's level, so a load off centre tilts it and water floods over the low edge.
ideas.form: A pond mini game with real floating; a film of a raft tipping over.

ideas.title: The island's coin
ideas.goal: Lumi strikes coins at the workshop: a blank of silver, a die with an owl and Lumi's face, one hammer blow; the player can strike a coin too and hand it to a friend, who keeps it. Fun: make a tiny real object with weight and shine.
ideas.idea: The coin's relief is the die's height field pressed into the blank by how hard the hammer hits (a soft blow gives a shallow, half struck coin); Hikari's silver conductor shows every edge. Coins are tossed, roll and spin to rest on the ground like Euler's disk.
ideas.form: A workshop tool and traced macro shots of a coin spinning down.

ideas.title: Rocks that ring
ideas.goal: Every rock on the island has its own note: the player hits rocks with a stick and finds the ones that make a tune. Fun: an instrument you find, not one you are given.
ideas.idea: The note comes from the rock's real shape: the lowest vibration modes of its mesh (FEM eigenvalues for granite) set the pitch and decay, and the hit shows the mode as a shimmer over the surface.
ideas.form: A sound and physics feature; a film of Lumi playing a rock pile.

ideas.title: Stars to sail by
ideas.goal: On clear nights the sky shows the real stars of the island's latitude and season, turning through the night; a lost friend at sea finds home by the player pointing at the right star. Fun: the sky becomes a map.
ideas.idea: A star catalogue (bright stars with magnitude and colour) placed by sidereal time; the Milky Way as a faint band; the tracer shows stars as tiny lights reflected in the calm sea.
ideas.form: Rendering of the night sky; a traced still of the sky over the sea.

ideas.title: Sand that blows
ideas.goal: Wind moves the beach: ripples, little dunes that creep, footprints filled in after a gust. The player builds a wall and watches sand pile behind it. Fun: shape the land and let the wind finish it.
ideas.idea: A saltation height field on the GPU (Werner's dune model: slabs hop downwind, avalanche past the angle of repose), driven by the island's wind.
ideas.form: A beach simulation; a time lapse traced film.

ideas.title: Camera obscura, sharp
ideas.goal: The player walks into the dark hut and sees the island on the wall, upside down and sharp enough to see friends walking. Fun: a room-sized camera you stand inside.
ideas.idea: A deeper hut and a real lens designed with GeometricalOptics.jl (focal length to the wall), traced at 2048 spp.
ideas.form: Project camera-obscura's next step; a traced still.
